interpretation_boundaries: TTL is applied only to seen-but-unreviewed cases; fraud labels do not drive expiry or queue selection.
A case is eligible at step t when t-arrival_step is no greater than the declared TTL. Expiry occurs before refresh-time rescoring, so finite TTL can reduce release workload.
All TTLs use the same balanced rolling systems, rescore-on-refresh handoff rule, continuous 50 reviews/10k entitlement and deterministic non-label tie-break.

The predeclared detection guardrail is no worse than 2 percentage points versus infinite TTL separately for precision, fraud recall and fraud-value recall. The workload target is at least 50% fewer refresh-time rescores.
The operational_candidate field is a deterministic frontier screen, not a statistical promotion decision and not a production recommendation.
The infinite TTL must reproduce the v1.13 rescore_pending result when the main-branch reference file is available.

PaySim is synthetic; dataset steps are not production SLA units, transaction amount is not prevented loss, and the upstream rolling lifecycle still assumes prior-period labels are available at refresh.
